overall: The AG found the Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law because a significant portion of its April 15 meeting was inaccessible to the public due to overcrowding and inaudibility, ordered future compliance, and declined to review the public hearing notice claim.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 15 meeting was inaccessible: the room could not hold the crowd and attendees could not hear the proceedings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that a portion of the Board’s April 15 meeting was inaccessible to the public, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint also noted a deficiency in the legal notice for a public hearing held during the April 15 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to review whether notice for the public hearing was sufficient.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no additional remedial action ordered because a complete recording of the April 15 meeting is online).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
